Al Jazeera (Al Jazeera Staff) — "Hegseth to cut number of US general and admiral positions by 20%". Published 30 September 2026. CONFIRMED 30 Sep.
Retrieved via WebFetch. Facts and quotes as returned by the tool.

WHAT: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth will cut general and admiral positions by 20 percent — doubling the 10 percent reduction he ordered last year. Affects roughly 800 flag and general officer positions across Army, Navy and Air Force. To be completed by 1 January 2027.
WHERE/WHEN ANNOUNCED: Wednesday 30 September at Marine Corps Base Quantico, Virginia, in Hegseth's "State of the Force" address to junior officers and enlisted personnel.
SOURCING IN THE ARTICLE: "a Pentagon official has told Al Jazeera"; the roughly-800-positions and 1 Jan 2027 detail attributed to the Associated Press citing Pentagon officials.
IMPORTANT: the cut applies to BILLETS (positions designated for generals and admirals), not an order to remove 20% of serving officers.

DIRECT QUOTES (verbatim as returned):
Senator Jack Reed (Democrat, Rhode Island; ranking member, Senate Armed Services Committee):
"Congress has been clear with the Secretary that he must consult this body and explain his reasoning for senior officer removals and promotion holds. To date, we have not received satisfactory answers."
"Our military is conducting major operations around the world, and the force is already under strain."

Pete Hegseth, stated rationale from his May 2025 memo: the aim was to free the military from "unnecessary bureaucratic layers".

CONTEXT FROM THE ARTICLE: the administration has removed over two dozen military leaders since January 2025, including the Army's top uniformed officer and the only two four-star female officers.

CROSS-CHECK (approved): BBC News, "Hegseth soon to announce more firings among US military's top ranks", by Brandon Drenon, URL https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crq5xvnq8yzqo , published 30 September 2026 15:19 GMT (16:19 BST). BBC frames it as "expected to announce ... according to US media" and notes that at the September 2025 Quantico gathering Hegseth criticised the department as too "woke" and said "fat generals and admirals" is "a bad look".
